page: Amazon Web Services m6i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture, offering 4 dedicated vCPUs spread across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a 3.5 GHz clock speed. System memory totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The server includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic instruction sets like AES and SHA-NI. It does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, and it provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that the server delivers average single-thread processing alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to its 4-vCPU scale. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 1885.19 and Geekbench single-core scored 1434.0, both falling within the middle 50% benchmark band. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 27.93 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression yielded 9.94 GB/sec, also displaying average tiers. Conversely, parallel metrics such as multi-core stress-ng (3857.84), Geekbench multi-core (3127.0), and PassMark CPU (5841.81) remain in the bottom 25%. Uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths achieved 29.35 GB/sec and 24.45 GB/sec, respectively.

With a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware configuration offers a balanced resource profile for routine operational tasks. The primary technical tradeoff centers on its bounded CPU scale and reliance on remote EBS storage, which restricts heavy multi-threaded compute and data-intensive batch execution. In application testing, the instance achieved a static web serving throughput of 6.51 GB/sec and 3.93 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. It is best configured for mid-tier web serving, application middleware, small caching layers, development environments, and moderate general-purpose business logic.
